installation.note: parted is commonly available by default on Linux systems

overview.summary: parted creates and manipulates partition tables (GPT and MBR) and can resize partitions. It supports scripting (parted script) and is often preferred over fdisk for GPT and for non-interactive use. Use with care; partitioning can cause data loss.
when_to_use: Create GPT or MBR partition tables

syntax.description: parted DEVICE enters interactive mode. With COMMAND(s), it runs non-interactively. Always specify the disk device (e.g., /dev/sda).
examples: sudo parted /dev/sdb mklabel gpt mkpart primary 0% 100%

options.description: List partition layout on all block devices

examples.title: List partition tables
examples.description: Show partition layout for all disks

examples.title: Create GPT and one partition
examples.command: sudo parted -s /dev/sdb mklabel gpt mkpart primary 0% 100%
examples.description: Create GPT table and one partition using whole disk (example)

common_pitfalls.description: Partitioning the wrong disk or misreading units (MiB vs MB) can destroy data.
common_pitfalls.solution: Confirm device with lsblk; use unit MiB in parted for clarity; back up critical data.
